summary: W4 grag-seed-retrieval handoff: deliver only relevance-discovery semantic seeds for Element, Relationship, and View channels. Each channel has an independent release threshold, returns every candidate meeting that channel gate, allows valid zero-result outcomes, and excludes graph closure, traversal expansion, neighborhood closure, and downstream graph-completion behavior from this stage.
notes: Selected viewpoint frame: Application Usage Viewpoint. Stakeholder concern: application architects, requirements owners, implementation designers, and acceptors need seed retrieval behavior to be independently observable per canonical object channel before any closure application function runs. Purpose: designing, deciding, and handoff preparation.

Affected View rationale: no View membership changed. grag-seed-closure-usage remains contextual Application Usage architecture for the later retrieval-to-closure chain, while this handoff scope is only grag-seed-retrieval and does not authorize closure implementation. grag-delivery-impact-retrieval remains delivery sequencing context; downstream ImplementationDesign must scope this handoff to grag-seed-retrieval only.

Mutation summary: updated only grag-seed-retrieval. The element now states that W4 delivers only relevance-discovery semantic seeds for Element, ArchitectureRelationship, and View, with independent channel thresholds, all qualifying candidates returned, zero results allowed, no global cross-channel ranking, and no graph closure/traversal/neighborhood/downstream-completion output in this stage.

Coverage proof: grag-seed-retrieval functionalPoint.DT-04-three-channel-seed-discovery -> ExplicitAcceptanceTestcase-DT-04; grag-seed-retrieval functionalPoint.DT-05-threshold-all-correctness -> ExplicitAcceptanceTestcase-DT-05. Both mounted testcases stay under the exact grag-seed-retrieval element and use tests/explicit/entries/runIndependentSemanticSeeds.js.

Dependency-subgraph proof: focus element grag-seed-retrieval is the only implementation target in this handoff. Relevant context relationships are grag-rel-w31-w4 as upstream delivery gate, grag-rel-validation-seeds as the validated-query trigger into seed retrieval, and grag-rel-w4-seed-retrieval as W4 realization of seed retrieval. The downstream grag-rel-seeds-closure relationship is intentionally excluded from the handoff because closure begins after relevance seed discovery.

Acceptance boundary DT-04: the observable result exposes separate Element, Relationship, and View seed channels. Relationship and View seeds must be directly discoverable and independently attributed, not inferred through Element-only retrieval, traversal expansion, neighborhood closure, or graph completion.

Acceptance boundary DT-05: Element, Relationship, and View each have their own threshold gate. Every candidate at or above its channel threshold is returned, candidates below threshold are not released by that gate, unrelated queries may return zero results, and ANN top-k output is performance comparison only.

Human approval evidence: the 2026-07-25 user requirement explicitly requested grag-seed-retrieval, DT-04 and DT-05 acceptance mapping, independent Element/Relationship/View gates, all passing candidates returned, valid zero results, and no graph closure mixed into this stage. The handoff schema does not allow an approvedByHuman field, so global approval is recorded in this schema-compliant note and testcase approval is recorded as acceptanceApproval.DT-04 and acceptanceApproval.DT-05 attributes on grag-seed-retrieval.

Downstream ImplementationDesign should define contracts and explicit entrypoint ownership around tests/explicit/entries/runIndependentSemanticSeeds.js without adding graph closure, traversal expansion, neighborhood closure, or graph-completion obligations to this W4 seed retrieval handoff.
